mind_map.root_node: Angles as Turns (Rotational Motion, Degree Measurement & Geometry)

main_branches.branch_title: 1. Concept of Angle & Classification by Degree

sub_branches.sub_title: Anatomy of an Angle & Arm Invariance
key_nodes: Angle Definition: Figure formed by two rays (arms) sharing a common endpoint (vertex)
Rotational Measure: Angle represents degree of turn or opening between two arms, not arm lengths
Arm Invariance Principle: Extending or shortening arm length does not alter angle magnitude
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Believing a drawn angle with longer arm lines is larger than an angle with shorter arm lines.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Angle Measure = Amount of rotation required to turn one arm onto the other about vertex.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Adjusting scissors opening, door hinges, and laptop screens.

key_nodes: Right Angle: Exactly 90° (Quarter turn / 'L' shape corner)
Acute Angle: Greater than 0° and strictly less than 90° (Sharp corner, e.g., 30°, 45°, 60°)
Obtuse Angle: Strictly greater than 90° and less than 180° (Wide opening, e.g., 120°, 135°)
Straight Angle: Exactly 180° (Half turn / straight line)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Classifying a rotated right angle as acute or obtuse simply because its arms are not horizontal/vertical.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Classification Criteria: Acute < 90°; Right = 90°; 90° < Obtuse < 180°; Straight = 180°.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Architectural roof pitch, body postures in Yoga/gymnastics, and paper folding.

main_branches.branch_title: 2. Turns as Fractional Circles & Clock Geometry

key_nodes: Full Rotation / Full Turn: 360° (Complete circular turn back to start)
Half Turn (1/2 turn): 180° (Straight angle)
Quarter Turn (1/4 turn): 90° (Right angle)
Eighth Turn (1/8 turn): 45° (Half of right angle)
Protractor Scale: Semi-circular tool calibrated from 0° to 180° for exact degree measurement
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Reading wrong inner/outer scale on protractor by aligning baseline incorrectly.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Degree Turn = Fractional Turn x 360° (e.g., 1/4 x 360° = 90°).
sub_branches.real_world_application: Wheel alignments, crane boom rotations, and robotic arm programming.

key_nodes: Clock Face Division: 360° full turn divided into 12 equal hour gaps
Hourly Radial Spacing: Each hour mark on clock represents exactly 30° (360° / 12 = 30°)
Clock Hands Angles: 1:00 = 30°; 2:00 = 60°; 3:00 = 90° (Right); 6:00 = 180° (Straight)
Minute Hand Speed: Minute hand turns 360° in 60 minutes -> 6° per minute
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Thinking minute hand at 12 and hour hand at 6 forms a 90° angle instead of 180°.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Clock Hand Angle = Difference in Hour Marks x 30°.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Analog clock reading and nautical navigational clock tracking.

key_nodes: Four Main Cardinal Directions: North (N), East (E), South (S), West (W)
Right-Angle Spacing: Adjacent cardinal directions are at 90° to each other (N-E, E-S, S-W, W-N)
Intermediate Directions: North-East (NE), South-East (SE), South-West (SW), North-West (NW)
45° Intermediate Spacing: Intermediate directions bisect 90° cardinal gaps into 45° angles
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Confusing clockwise (rightwards) rotation with anti-clockwise (leftwards) rotation direction.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Direction Rotations: 90° turn = Next cardinal point; 180° turn = Opposite cardinal point.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Aviation flight path headings, magnetic compass reading, and marching drills.
